The story is tightly unified around the themes of mortality, memory, and emotional risk. The beginning establishes Arthur’s emotional detachment—stemming from his past as an actuary and the loss of his brother—which caused his wife, Clara, to leave him. The middle introduces the inciting incident (finding the fatal car crash), which forces Arthur to confront the suddenness of death and the "extravagant waste" of unshared memories and rationed affection. Every detail, from the spilled contents of the woman's tote bag to Arthur's monologue, propels his internal arc forward. This logically leads to the satisfying conclusion, where Arthur overcomes his lifelong emotional cowardice, physically connects with the deceased woman so she isn't alone, and resolves to reach out to his ex-wife before it is too late.
